newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's GSM tender on track despite reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Romania's GSM tender on track despite reshuffle.

text.p: Plans by Romania's communications ministry to launch a tender for two GSM mobile telephone licences will not be hit by a government reshuffle, an official said.

On Monday, the country's ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) threw the nationalist Romanian National Unity Party (PUNR) -- which has four cabinet jobs, including the communications portfolio -- out of the governing coalition.
"The GSM tender is not in danger or subject to political moves. Everything will go on as planned. All deadlines will be observed," a senior ministry official told Reuters.
The PDSR said the move was in retaliation for the PUNR's recent attacks against President Ion Iliescu over a friendship treaty with neighbouring Hungary.
The ministry has already pushed back the closing date for the tender for the two GSM networks by two months to September 26 to give the applicants more time to consider their terms.

The GSM project, estimated to cost around $1 billion, is already running well behind schedule because of a shortage of free channels on the 900 MHz waveband, used mainly by the country's military and air force.
Political turmoil in the ministry last year also added to the problems.
Communications Minister Ovidiu Muntean was "still analysing" the PDSR's move but his resignation was almost certain, said the ministry official, who asked not to be named.
"His (Munteanu's) problem is that last year he defected from the ranks of PDSR to join the PUNR. I can't see him doing it now the other way round," the official said.

PDSR was angered by the calls of PUNR president Gheorghe Funar, who also plans to run in the presidential polls due on November 3, for Iliescu to be impeached for agreeing a much-delayed frienship treaty with Hungary which is vital for both countries' ambitions to join the European Union and NATO. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
